chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, and Uthman ibn Isa, from Ali ibn Salim, who said:
Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) said: 'Fear adultery, for it obliterates sustenance and invalidates the Religion.'
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and material consequences of adultery according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam Musa al-Kazim (peace be upon him) links the physical and spiritual consequences of zina, noting that it erodes sustenance (rizq) and invalidates religious standing (din). This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on zina as a 'major sin' that disrupts both worldly blessings and spiritual integrity, often cited in discussions of divine retribution and moral purification.
